question: What is the primary goal of using aseptic technique during a midwifery procedure?

options.A: To remove all normal flora permanently from the mother's skin
options.B: To prevent germs from entering a sterile wound or body site
options.C: To cure an existing deep tissue infection without using drugs
options.D: To completely sterilize the air inside the delivery ward

explanation: Aseptic technique creates a barrier to stop harmful micro-organisms from getting into clean areas of the body. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is the main difference between sterility and asepsis?

options.A: There is no practical difference between the two terms in daily clinical work
options.B: Sterility can be achieved with soap and water, while asepsis requires an autoclave
options.C: Asepsis applies only to surgical instruments, while sterility applies only to human skin
options.D: Sterility means zero living organisms, while asepsis means freedom from infectious material

explanation: Sterility is absolute, meaning completely free of all microbial life, whereas asepsis focuses on preventing the spread of infection-causing agents. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h1)

question: What action must you take immediately if you are unsure whether a sterile instrument has been contaminated?

options.A: Use it only if the patient has a strong immune system
options.B: Hold it over a flame for ten seconds before use
options.C: Treat it as contaminated and do not use it
options.D: Wipe it down quickly with methylated spirit

explanation: Safety rules state that any doubt about sterility means the item must be rejected to protect the patient. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why is turning your back on an open sterile tray considered a breach of technique?

options.A: The sterile items will automatically cool down and attract moisture
options.B: Air currents from behind travel faster and carry heavy bacteria
options.C: You can no longer monitor it to ensure it remains uncontaminated
options.D: Hospital regulations require midwives to face instrument trays at all times

explanation: Unwatched sterile fields can easily be accidentally touched or contaminated by passing colleagues or movement without your knowledge. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which part of an open sterile drape or field is safely considered non-sterile?

options.A: The exact center of the tray
options.B: The bottom layer resting on the table
options.D: The metallic handles of the forceps

explanation: The edges are easily touched or compromised during handling, so the outer margin is always treated as contaminated. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why must a midwife gather all dressing equipment before starting the procedure?

options.A: To comply with local laws regarding the storage of surgical cotton
options.B: To allow the cleaning solution enough time to evaporate in the air
options.C: To ensure the hospital inventory book balances at the end of the shift
options.D: To prevent leaving the patient unattended or breaking the sterile field later

explanation: Leaving a sterile setup to fetch forgotten items risks contamination and compromises patient safety. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h3)

question: In which direction should you wipe a surgical wound when cleaning it with antiseptic swabs?

options.B: From the bottom to the top

explanation: Cleaning from the cleanest area (the wound center) to the dirtiest area (surrounding skin) prevents pushing skin bacteria into the healing tissue. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the correct action regarding gloves when transitioning from removing an old dressing to cleaning the wound?

options.A: Keep the same gloves on since you are working on the same patient
options.B: Wipe the dirty gloves thoroughly with spirit and continue working
options.C: Take off the gloves and perform the rest of the procedure barehanded
options.D: Remove dirty gloves, perform hand hygiene, and put on new gloves

explanation: Old dressings carry micro-organisms from the wound surface, requiring glove removal and hand hygiene to stop cross-contamination. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h4)

question: Where should you safely dispose of used surgical blades and suture needles after a dressing procedure?

options.B: In an open plastic basin on the trolley
options.C: Wrapped inside the used cotton gauze
options.D: Inside the black domestic waste bin

explanation: Sharps must always go into a rigid safety box to prevent accidental needle-stick injuries to staff and cleaners. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why is it dangerous to recap used needles after a medical procedure?

options.A: It makes the needle too blunt to use on the next patient
options.B: It exposes the sterile medication inside to room air
options.C: Hospital administrative policies forbid keeping needles in trays
options.D: It greatly increases the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries

explanation: Trying to guide a cap back onto a used needle often results in piercing your own finger, exposing you to blood-borne infections. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why should you avoid pointing the tips of sterile forceps downward during a procedure?

options.A: The metal weight will cause the forceps to bend out of shape
options.B: Hospital protocol requires forceps to be held completely flat
options.C: It makes it difficult for your assistant to see the instrument
options.D: Contaminated liquids can flow down from your hands onto the sterile tips

explanation: Gravity pulls fluids downward; pointing tips down allows unsterile sweat or solution from your hands to contaminate the working end. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following actions is NOT safe when maintaining a sterile field?

options.A: Checking that the under-surface of the drape is dry
options.B: Keeping your hands positioned above your waist level
options.C: Reaching directly across an open sterile dressing pack
options.D: Discarding any instrument that touches an unsterile zone

explanation: Reaching across a sterile field risks shedding unnoticeable skin flakes or brushing the area with unsterile clothing. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h6)
